title: The spare-change sweep: a Friday ritual that fills the pig
description: Coins in coat pockets, the bottom of bags, the car door pocket — loose change leaks out of every budget unnoticed. The sweep gathers it once a week, on purpose, before it evaporates.

body.heading: Set up the sweep station
paragraphs: Put one piggy bank or jar somewhere you pass when you come home — by the door, on the dresser, beside the keys bowl. The location is the whole system: a savings jar in a cupboard is a savings jar forgotten.
Choose your sweep day and keep it fixed; Friday works well because it catches the whole week's pockets. Fixed beats frequent — a ritual you keep beats a resolution you admire.

body.heading: Run the Friday sweep
paragraphs: Empty every pocket, bag and coin tray into the jar, without keeping any coin back for luck. Add one small upgrade when the habit feels easy: sweep notes below a set value too, or round the jar's contents up to the nearest five with a transfer from your account.

When the jar fills, bank it the same week and write the total on a card kept beside the jar: jar one, jar two, running total. Watching the card fill is the reward that keeps the sweep alive — and the money, gathered from coins you never missed, is real.

takeaway: One jar by the door, one fixed sweep day, every coin in: bank each full jar, keep a running-total card, and let small change become visible money.
materials: A piggy bank or jar placed where you come in
A card and pen for the running total
supervision: No supervision is required; households may appoint one person as the jar's banker who records each banked total.
safetyNotes: Keep the jar out of reach of small children — coins are a choking hazard for toddlers.
Count and bank full jars promptly rather than keeping large amounts of cash in the home.
